From 8c88181ed452707f3815827225517b1964463b95 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jesper Dangaard Brouer <brouer@redhat.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Feb 2018 12:48:12 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] bpf: Sync kernel ABI header with tooling header for
 bpf_common.h

I recently fixed up a lot of commits that forgot to keep the tooling
headers in sync.  And then I forgot to do the same thing in commit
cb5f7334d479 ("bpf: add comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes"). Let correct
that before people notice ;-).

Lawrence did partly fix/sync this for bpf.h in commit d6d4f60c3a09
("bpf: add selftest for tcpbpf").

Fixes: cb5f7334d479 ("bpf: add comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes")
Signed-off-by: Jesper Dangaard Brouer <brouer@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>

diff --git a/tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h b/tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h
index 18be90725ab0..ee97668bdadb 100644
--- a/tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h
+++ b/tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h
@@ -15,9 +15,10 @@
 
 /* ld/ldx fields */
 #define BPF_SIZE(code)  ((code) & 0x18)
-#define		BPF_W		0x00
-#define		BPF_H		0x08
-#define		BPF_B		0x10
+#define		BPF_W		0x00 /* 32-bit */
+#define		BPF_H		0x08 /* 16-bit */
+#define		BPF_B		0x10 /*  8-bit */
+/* eBPF		BPF_DW		0x18    64-bit */
 #define BPF_MODE(code)  ((code) & 0xe0)
 #define		BPF_IMM		0x00
 #define		BPF_ABS		0x20
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h`**
   - Added comments to the definitions of `BPF_W`, `BPF_H`, and `BPF_B` to clarify their sizes:
     - `BPF_W` is now commented as "32-bit".
     - `BPF_H` is now commented as "16-bit".
     - `BPF_B` is now commented as "8-bit".
   - Added a comment for `BPF_DW` indicating it represents "64-bit" with the corresponding value `0x18`.

### Relationships
- The modifications in `bpf_common.h` are intended to synchronize the kernel ABI header with the tooling header, addressing an oversight from a previous commit (cb5f7334d479) that added comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes but did not update the tooling header accordingly. This patch ensures consistency between the kernel and tooling headers, which is crucial for maintaining compatibility and clarity in the BPF (Berkeley Packet Filter) implementation.

bpf: Sync kernel ABI header with tooling header for
 bpf_common.h

I recently fixed up a lot of commits that forgot to keep the tooling
headers in sync.  And then I forgot to do the same thing in commit
cb5f7334d479 ("bpf: add comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes"). Let correct
that before people notice ;-).

Lawrence did partly fix/sync this for bpf.h in commit d6d4f60c3a09

Fixes: cb5f7334d479 ("bpf: add comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes")
Signed-off-by: Jesper Dangaard Brouer <brouer@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug was the failure to keep the tooling header (`bpf_common.h`) in sync with the kernel ABI header after a previous commit that added comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes. This oversight led to inconsistencies in the definitions and comments related to BPF sizes, which could cause confusion and potential errors in the usage of these constants in BPF-related code.

Here is the patch:
 /* ld/ldx fields */
 #define BPF_SIZE(code)  ((code) & 0x18)
-#define		BPF_W		0x00
-#define		BPF_H		0x08
-#define		BPF_B		0x10
+#define		BPF_W		0x00 /* 32-bit */
+#define		BPF_H		0x08 /* 16-bit */
+#define		BPF_B		0x10 /*  8-bit */
+/* eBPF		BPF_DW		0x18    64-bit */
 #define BPF_MODE(code)  ((code) & 0xe0)
 #define		BPF_IMM		0x00

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
#define BPF_W		0x00
#define BPF_H		0x08
#define BPF_B		0x10
```
Reason:
These definitions for BPF sizes were not updated to include comments that clarify their bit sizes after a previous commit. This inconsistency between the tooling header and the kernel ABI header could lead to confusion and errors when developers use these constants in BPF-related code, as they may not understand the intended sizes without proper documentation.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#define BPF_W		0x00 /* 32-bit */
#define BPF_H		0x08 /* 16-bit */
#define BPF_B		0x10 /*  8-bit */
```
Reason:
The added comments next to each BPF size definition provide clear documentation on the bit sizes associated with each constant. This synchronization with the kernel ABI header ensures that developers have the correct information, reducing the likelihood of confusion and potential errors in the usage of these constants in BPF-related code.
